name: 1611 Prairie Avenue — the lost frame pair with 1609, K16 clapboard

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The house claims the 1904 target and no more: Robinson 1886 plate 10 draws the pair and the T-1840 census carries it to 1904 on the supplied expert guidance (backcast_1886). The 1911 sheet draws the 1607-1611 loft in its place, so the pair was gone by then; when it was built and when it came down are not read, and no building date is claimed.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 13.750, v 2.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the plate: the plate's fit is 4.54 m RMS, the weakest of the four T-1250 fits (a photographed atlas page, rotated and curved toward the binding), plus about a pixel (0.35 m) of reading. Rotation 179.605 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 1611 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1607 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: RECONSTRUCTED: Robinson's atlas prints no storey count, and the 1911 sheet, which would, draws the loft that replaced the pair. Two storeys is the register's 'modest frame facade, timber cornice, sash windows' read as a two-storey house; built as the kit's two storeys of sash under the cornice.

construction.note: Robinson 1886 colours the pair yellow, the plate's frame (its brick buildings are pink, as the pair on lot 7 next south is); the register's 'pre-1911 paired frame house' agrees. Built board by board from the K16 timber kit at a frame wall's 0.15 m, never with a masonry wall's thickness.

frame_house.note: The whole house from the K16 kit (T-1867), one half of a pair. READ off Robinson 1886 plate 10 through the draft's fit of the trace r1886-1611-f: the main body's rectangle (10.5 m deep, 5.25 m along Prairie, the footprint below) and the line the plate draws between 1611 and 1609, here the party wall (`party_wall`): neither half builds it, so the pair stands as one frame block with one continuous front, rear and cornice, and each record closes its own outer side. Everything else is RECONSTRUCTED from the kit and recorded as L-k16-1609-1611-frame-pair-1867: clapboard on a water table over a 0.45 m foundation, corner boards at the outer corners, two-over-two sash in flat timber casings (a door and two windows below, three windows above on the front, three a storey on the outer side, the rear's own pattern), a four-panel door at the outer end of the front (the draft's entrance side, the pair's doors at its ends), the deep frieze under a boxed eave with scroll brackets as the register's 'timber cornice', a flat roof behind it, one brick stack at the party wall, and a small kit porch over the door with its timber steps as the register's 'bounded stoop'.

roof_covering.note: No roof covering has been read for the pair. A flat roof behind a timber cornice on a Chicago frame house of the period was commonly laid in tar and gravel; the covering and its dark grey are RECONSTRUCTED and not modelled beyond the deck's colour.

boundary.note: T-3230 (piece 2 of T-3216; the owner, 2026-10-27: every worked house's walk to its door and its front boundaries, and where no picture shows them a stated reconstruction consistent with the block). No picture of this front is held. The east side of the 1600 block is drawn open where it is drawn at all: 1621's and 1623's 1886 drawings and 1625's 1890 photograph show no fence or kerb on the street line (T-3221), and 1613, 1615 and 1619, unpictured, were laid open on that reading (T-3229). So this front is laid open too (`layout: open`, archetypes/k16_yard.py): nothing on the street line, the whole front between the lot lines the opening. The 1911 sheet draws 1611 and its party-wall twin 1609 on one parcel, prairie_1607 (data/street_grid/1904.json), carried into the house's plan frame by the placement its sidecar holds (the transform that puts 1720's recorded street line, u 31.2, back on its parcel to the centimetre): the street line runs u 14.55 at the parcel's north line to 14.46 at its south, taken as u 14.47 where the walk meets it, on the porch stair's axis (s 4.25). The lot's north side is the party wall with 1609 (s -0.025); its south side is put on the house's own south wall (s 5.25), which stands 0.44 m past the parcel's south line (s 4.81) as the house was fitted, within the sheet's 3.08 m fit residual. RECONSTRUCTED: that the front stood open in 1904 (liberty L-k16-walks-1600-block-3230).

yard.note: T-3230. A front walk in flags straight out from the porch stair's foot (read off the built steps) to the street line, the public walk's inner edge, 1.2 m wide in 0.9 m flags 0.06 m over the ground, the district's K14 walk sizes and the width 1613, 1615 and 1619 were given (T-3229). RECONSTRUCTED: the walk's line, width and surface; no picture shows them (liberty L-k16-walks-1600-block-3230). No lawn is laid: the yard's ground is the app's own (generators/archetypes/k16_yard.py).

function.note: The 1911 sheet draws a 1911 loft at 1607-1611, not a 1904 building. The T-1840 census (frontage-20-024, backcast_1886) stands the lot-6 frame pair for 1904 on the supplied expert guidance (named record pa-1611-1904-correction) because Robinson 1886 plate 10 prints 1611 against the south half of it. There is no 1904 directory listing at the address; residence is inferred from the register's 'pre-1911 paired frame house'.

citations.citation: Robinson, E. Robinson's Atlas of the City of Chicago. New York: E. Robinson, 1886. Plate 10, "Part of 2.39.14 Assessors Div."

Lot and subdivision lines, and the outlines of the houses at 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie that Glessner House names as standing in 1904 and gone by 1911
what_it_does_not_supply: Street widths: its bands are not drawn to the widths it prints (Prairie printed 66, drawn about 55 ft)
Anything as of 1904 on its own authority

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 20.
what_it_supplies: The Illinois Central / Michigan Central right-of-way and, from the 16th Street row south about 60 m, the water's edge beside it, as of 1911
Footprints, lot lines, street widths (66 ft; 16th Street 50 ft), addresses, material by colour and story counts for Indiana Av. to the tracks, 16th to 18th Street, as of 1911
Its own printed Scale of Feet, which the georeference uses as its scale
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-1867 refines the district draft (T-2335) in place under the same id: 1611 is the south half of the lot-6 frame pair Robinson 1886 plate 10 draws, rebuilt whole from the K16 timber kit as one of two two-storey frame houses on a shared party wall with 1609 — clapboard built board by board on a water table, cased two-over-two sash and a panelled door, a deep frieze under a bracketed boxed eave carried across both fronts as one timber cornice, a flat roof behind it, a brick stack at the party wall, and a small kit porch with timber steps at the south end of the front, so the pair's doors stand at its outer ends. What is read: the plan of each half and the line between them off Robinson 1886 plate 10 (r1886-1609-f, r1886-1611-f, carried by the plate's T-1250 fit), frame construction from the plate's yellow, and the pair's survival to 1904 from the T-1840 census (backcast_1886, the supplied expert guidance). Everything else is reconstructed and recorded as L-k16-1609-1611-frame-pair-1867. 1607 is not a house: '1607-1611' is the address range of the four-storey loft the 1911 sheet draws over lots 5-6, which replaced the pair after 1904, so no 1904 building stands under 1607 and the loft is not back-projected. No photograph, print or description of either house has been found: the Prairie library's one picture at the address (a16-cgy-1609-loft-1910, searched 2026-10-12) shows the 1910 E. T. Cade loft that replaced the pair; one that turns up replaces the kit's choices here.
